newsitem.title: USA: Tele-Comms CEO Malone says he is at helm.
newsitem.headline: Tele-Comms CEO Malone says he is at helm.

text.p: Tele-Communications Chief executive John Malone on Thursday took the opportunity at a major cable trade show to reaffirm that he is actively heading up the giant cable company.
"I put on the cable operator uniform again about five weeks ago," Malone told the Western Show, a key cable television industry trade show.
Last week the company announced layoffs and said it would keep a keen eye on holding expenses down in a bid to lower its debt.

At the time analysts said they believed Malone took the actions to shore up TCI's stock price, which had been lingering near its 52-week lows. On Thursday it was quoted at 13-3/8, up 1/8. Its year low stood at 11-1/4.
Malone was speaking to industry leaders at a panel discussion that is one of the best attended events of the cable show.

Malone also talked about the need for the cable industry and TCI in particular to refocus its business strategy toward generating earnings as opposed to reinvesting its capital in infrastructure and new businesses.
Malone said the industry has the lowest return on invested capital and "that story gets a little old. It's time we started to think about getting good returns."

He said a company like TCI that generates $3 billion in cash should spend one-third on interest, one-third on capital expenditures and the remaining third should be retunred to shareholders or invested in new businesses.
But Malone said new business investment must generate a return. "That's where I'm trying to take TCI." Malone said.

TCI's first priority would be to focus on rolling out digital set-top boxes to its customers. Digital provides an opportunity to offer viewers the ability to perform functions such as surfing the Internet and accessing services like near-video on demand, he said.
Digital may also curb the threat of satellite-based TV, he said. Direct broadcast satellite has become a bigger competitive threat to cable TV than many had expected.
He also said that TCI has not given up on providing advanced services like telephony.

Malone said the company is still awaiting final determination on whether it will have to spin-off its Time Warner Inc stake. If TCI has to shed its Time Warner holdings it may do so as a spinoff, he said. TCI was a major holder of Turner before it merged with Time Warner. "If we can do so tax-efficiently, we will spin it off to shareholders."
